The story relies heavily on well-worn tropes and clichés of romantic melodrama. Setting an awkward reunion between estranged former partners in a café is a very common plot setup. Furthermore, the story uses numerous overused gestures and dialogue beats to signal tension: stirring a cup while looking out the window, keeping a jacket on to show reluctance to stay, an unanswered letter, a missed connection at a train station, a vague reference to a past "summer at the lake" ("Sommer am See"), and the classic "standing up to leave only to sit back down" ending. Because these elements are so familiar and predictable, the piece lacks originality.
